_comment: Seeded evidence history for the Valor demo profile. One JSON object per line; `day_offset` is days before the seed date, so the history is always relative to demo day. Fictional persona: Alex, L3 -> L4, checkout/payments. Deliberate demo hooks are marked with `_hook`.

statement: Threaded an idempotency key through the refund path so a redelivered provider webhook can't apply the same refund twice (PROJ-231, draft PR #419)
Answered Riley's two questions on PR #418 in the diff rather than in chat: why full jitter over decorrelated, and that the cap is per attempt not cumulative
Explained the retry-storm failure mode to the PM in the checkout sync in non-technical terms - when the provider slows down, our fixed-interval retries make it worse
Checkout weekly sync: #418 named the week's critical path because the platform transport migration (PROJ-248) is blocked on it; refund idempotency is next

Moved retry handling out of the payments client into the shared transport layer and replaced the fixed 2s interval with exponential backoff plus full jitter, capped at 30s / 5 attempts (PROJ-244, PR #418)
Decided the non-idempotent-verb check belongs in the transport rather than each caller, so a new caller cannot opt itself into retrying a POST by accident
Surfaced provider error codes in the checkout failure log, which is what made the retry storm legible in the first place (PROJ-238, PR #412)
Evening wrap-up: 2 items carried forward, session-cache risk flagged across two tickets touching the refund path
Reviewed platform-core#415 (shared transport skeleton) outside my own tickets and flagged that the retry layer sat one level too high; their design changed before it was built
Traced the checkout p99 regression to a synchronous address-validation call in the hot path; wrote up the trace on PROJ-259 before picking it up
Wrote the payments retry contract down for the platform team - attempts, cap, which verbs retry, who owns the budget (PROJ-241, PR #408)
Morning briefing: ranked the day against this week's goals, deep block reserved for the refund fix
Found the double-refund window: we ack the webhook after applying the refund, so a slow response looks like a delivery failure to the provider and it redelivers
Requested changes on the provider-adapter extraction (PR #410) - the interface leaked provider-specific error shapes to callers
1:1 with Sam: agreed retry policy moves to the transport layer, 5 attempts / 30s cap; L4 gap named as owning a problem area where the scope isn't already decided
Weekly reflection: strong execution week, light on industry-knowledge signals
Walked Dana through the payments provider's retry semantics and where our client diverged from them, after she hit the same confusion in review
On call: checkout error rate spiked when the provider degraded; drained the retry queue and shipped a temporary attempt cap, then filed PROJ-244 for the real fix rather than leaving the workaround in
Added the provider-degradation incident to the runbook with the exact queue-drain commands, so the next on-call doesn't rediscover them
Added an integration test that replays a duplicate webhook delivery end to end, which is the case the unit tests kept missing
Proposed that checkout PRs touching the payments provider carry a rollback note; the team adopted it as a checklist item
Aligned with the platform team on transport ownership before either side wrote code - avoided two competing retry implementations
Reviewed the webhook queue-client migration and caught a silent message-loss path on shutdown
Wrote the design for splitting provider adapters behind an interface: three options, chose the narrow one, explicitly punted multi-provider routing (PROJ-192)
Compared how three payment providers document retry and idempotency semantics, and used the strictest as our internal contract
Migrated checkout webhooks off the deprecated queue client without a maintenance window, behind a dual-read flag (PROJ-219, PR #389)
Ran a 20-minute team walkthrough of the new adapter interface and why callers should never see provider error shapes
Debugged a stuck capture queue during release; root cause was an unbounded retry on a non-idempotent call, which became the argument for the verb check in the transport
Documented the checkout failure taxonomy so support can distinguish provider declines from our own errors
Reviewed 6 PRs across checkout this sprint, including two outside my own tickets
Chose to make the refund path idempotent at the provider boundary rather than in our database, so a replay is safe even if our write succeeded and the ack didn't
Shipped idempotency keys on the charge path, including the key-collision case nobody had specified (PROJ-186, PR #341)
Negotiated the checkout / platform boundary for outbound HTTP with two staff engineers and wrote the outcome down the same day
Reproduced an intermittent capture failure that only appeared under connection reuse, and proved it was the provider closing idle sockets early
Wrote the on-call runbook for provider degradation from scratch - symptoms, dashboards, the three levers, when to page the provider (PROJ-205)
Paired with a new team member through their first checkout change and left them the mental model rather than the patch
Backfilled tests around the capture path before refactoring it, so the refactor had something to be safe against
Cut the checkout test suite from 11 to 6 minutes by fixing the fixture that rebuilt the provider sandbox per test
Drafted the webhook migration plan with an explicit rollback step per phase; reviewed by platform before any code was written
Chased a reconciliation mismatch to a timezone assumption in the settlement report and fixed the assumption, not the report
Ran the joint session with support to agree what checkout error copy should say for each provider decline reason
Gave a first-time contributor a review that named the pattern to follow and linked the example, instead of listing 14 line comments
Caught a partial-refund bug in staging that would have shipped, by replaying a week of real refund shapes against the new code
Evaluated whether to adopt the provider's new SDK; recommended staying on our thin client because the SDK hid the retry behaviour we need to control
Instrumented the checkout funnel with per-step timings, so the p99 conversation could start from data instead of impressions
_hook: no `role` on purpose - /valor-reflection should ask whether this was led or co-built before it goes in a review

statement: Rewrote the checkout onboarding doc after watching two new joiners get stuck on the same provider sandbox setup
Kept the settlement job single-threaded and documented why, after measuring that the bottleneck was the provider's rate limit rather than our CPU
Presented the checkout failure taxonomy at the engineering-wide demo, and support adopted the vocabulary in their macros
Delivered the first slice of the provider adapter split with the interface, one adapter, and the parity test harness
Fixed a flaky checkout test that had been retried in CI for months, by removing the shared clock it depended on
Mapped every outbound call in the checkout path and which ones lacked a timeout - the finding that started the transport work
